evidence.note: First real decomposition: a numbered list of subsystems (package/bin, CLI dev/build/start, Vite plugin, pages router SSR, app router, middleware...). It mirrors the requirement bullets and has an implied 'foundation-first' order but no explicit done-criteria per milestone — flat-list flavored (anchor 3-5 territory).

Reached a minimal end-to-end path early — dev server + basic pages rendering, then ran the suite for a 34/325 baseline before layering features. This 'thin vertical slice first, then layer' behavior and tying next work to concrete test buckets ('big targets: app router route handlers, pages') pushes above 5.

Sequencing was dependency-aware in spots (resolution/plugin/CLI before routing before SSR; got client navigation working to 'unlock ~20 tests') and each target explicitly tied to fixtures/test counts, an 8-flavored trait.

But subsystem interfaces were not explicitly managed: adding middleware regressed 73→25 because it consumed the request body — coupling surprised the agent rather than being planned for, forcing reactive backtracking rather than milestone re-planning.

Late trajectory shows greedy, test-count-driven target selection ('big bucket left is app router CSR') and repeated revert/re-add cycles (hydration reverts). Progress tracked as a running pass count (215→221) but never against an explicit milestone plan with done-criteria; decomposition stayed emergent, not a living milestone structure.

reasoning: The agent identified the major subsystems and picked a sensible dependency order (plugin/CLI → pages routing → SSR → app router → middleware/cache), and notably established a minimal end-to-end slice early and used the Playwright suite to gate each subsequent step — traits of the 8 anchor. However, the decomposition itself was a flat requirement-mirroring list without explicit per-milestone done-criteria, and sequencing after the baseline was greedy-by-test-bucket rather than a maintained dependency-aware milestone plan; interface coupling between subsystems was discovered through regressions (middleware body, hydration/templates) rather than deliberately managed. This lands solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 5, i.e. a 6.
